newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-ATLANTE WIN AFTER GOALKEEPER GOES INTO ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLANTE WIN AFTER GOALKEEPER GOES INTO ATTACK.

text.p: Atlante, the overall leaders of the Mexican championship, grabbed a last-minute win on Sunday after sending goalkeeper Jorge Campos into attack.

Atlante coach Miguel Mejia Baron, frustrated at his forwards' failure to break through the defence of lowly UAG, brought on the reserve goalkeeper in the second half and sent first-choice goalkeeper Jorge Campos into attack.
The gamble paid off when Atlante finally broke down an obstinate UAG defence with an injury time goal by Mexico's Brazilian-born international striker Zague.

Mexican international Campos, a former surfer who is famous for his outrageous luminous pink and green goalkeeping kits, joined Atlante after playing for Los Angeles Galaxy in the inaugural Major League Soccer tournament in the United States.
He has already played in attack several times in his career and in one Galaxy game he set up a goal with a spectacular donkey kick.
Atlante's 1-0 win kept them top of group one and they are also the team with most points overall in the competition.

Uruguayan coach Carlos Miloc was sent off on his debut in charge of group two leaders Leon after being involved in an altercation with Toluca defender Efrain Herrera. Miloc at one stage pushed the referee. Leon won 3-2.
Traditional favourites America, who are having one of their worst seasons ever, lost for the sixth time in 13 games when they were beaten 2-1 by Atlas.
Cameroon veteran Francois Omam-Biyik scored the only goal for America, who are third in group two.
The 18 teams play each other once but are divided into four groups with eight qualifying for the play-offs.
